text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali says Companies Law passed by parliament last month cannot be ratified before the securities law is also passed.
- 16 Jordanian companies have won contracts under U.N. oil-for-food deal to export goods to Iraq including medicine, manufactured goods, vegetable oils and soap with a total value of $52 million.
- Central Bank assets fell at the end of March to 3.14 billion dinars ($4.44 billion) from 3.16 billion in February.
- National Party merges into new National Constitutional Party.

- Buzz of activity at prime ministry on elections. Interior minister requests delay in changes to election law because of new developments. Moslem Brotherhood leader calls for guarantees of government neutrality in elections and assurance that the movement will not be sidelined in next parliament.
- Information minister says Jordan's relations with Syria have not reached a crisis, declines to comment on a question about new differences between Jordan and Syria.
- Defence lawyer for soldier who shot dead Israeli schoolgirls says he in good health and charges against him will be issued soon.
- Deputy Prime Minister Jawad Anani says Jordan is suffering from slow processing by U.N. of requests to export to Iraq under U.N. resolution 986.
- Cabinet sanctions execution of two convicted of murder.
